artifacts.summary: Draft MFA policy document shared for review

items.text:
## Summary

This memo records the current status of the draft multi‑factor authentication policy, outlines confidentiality requirements, and assigns next‑step actions for the legal‑product circle.

## Purpose and Current Status

The draft MFA policy uploaded to the restricted folder on 2026-01-28 incorporates the three edge‑case scenarios flagged by Vera Becker:
1. Potential two‑week renewal delay for accounts still on single‑factor login.
2. Risk to the 30‑day “early‑upgrade” incentive if MFA enrollment extends beyond the current window.
3. Legacy contracts lacking explicit MFA clauses that may need addenda.
Aarav Tanaka has merged these comments and prepared a revised version for the security team’s review. The go‑live date is set for **day 27 **, and the selected MFA provider is **SecureAuth (restricted folder)**.

## Confidentiality and Distribution Constraints

All copies of the policy – the original draft‑review, the revised version, and any subsequent comments – must remain in the **restricted folder** and be shared **only within the legal‑product circle**. 
- Do not forward the document outside this group until final sign‑off is obtained. 
- Jamal Osei has performed an initial review; his comments are logged in the same folder and are not to be disseminated beyond the CEO’s office.
- Any external vendor communication (e.g., with SecureAuth) should reference the provider name only in the context of the restricted folder and must not appear in any broader‑audience artifact.

## Next Steps and Action Items

- **Aarav Tanaka**: Please upload the revised draft to the restricted folder by end of day and tag the security lead for a quick triage.
- **Vera Becker**: Align the sales onboarding timeline with the go‑live date (day 27) and flag any renewal‑pipeline impacts that arise from the two‑week enrollment lag. Post any new concerns as comments on the draft.
- **Security Team (lead)**: Review the revised draft within 48 hours of receipt and confirm that SecureAuth integration details meet compliance standards.
- **Jamal Osei**: Provide final executive sign‑off after security validation; update the policy status in the project tracker.
All participants should record their completions in the shared tracking sheet located at **/shared/mfa_policy/tracker.xlsx**.

items.text:
## Description

We need to open a formal implementation ticket in the tracking system to coordinate the technical rollout of mandatory multi‑factor authentication (MFA) across all user accounts. The ticket will capture all required artifacts, deadlines, and owner responsibilities so the engineering and security teams can execute the go‑live on **day 27 **.

**Scope**
- Upload the revised MFA policy (currently stored in the restricted folder) and link it to the implementation ticket.
- Record the selected MFA provider **SecureAuth (restricted folder)** and any integration parameters.
- Define the enrollment window, noting the potential two‑week renewal delay for accounts still on single‑factor login as flagged by Vera Becker.
- Capture the “early‑upgrade” incentive risk and the need for addenda on legacy contracts.

**Owner**: Aarav Tanaka (General Counsel) will create the ticket, attach the policy documents, and tag the security lead for triage. The ticket will be visible only to the legal‑product circle and the security team until the rollout plan is finalized. Please keep this information within the legal‑product circle and do not forward it outside the restricted folder.

**Next Steps**
- Aarav to create the ticket **TKT-041-M1A3** by end of day and attach the policy from **/shared/mfa_policy/**.
- Security lead (Sofia Lopez) to review integration details within 48 hours of ticket creation.
- Vera Becker to monitor sales onboarding alignment and flag any renewal‑pipeline impacts directly on the ticket.
- Jamal Osei to provide executive sign‑off once security validation is complete.

## Acceptance criteria

- Implementation ticket exists in the system with ID **TKT-041-M1A3** and is linked to the policy document stored in the restricted folder.
- All required owners (Aarav Tanaka, Security lead, Vera Becker) are tagged and have acknowledged the ticket.
- Integration details for **SecureAuth (restricted folder)** are documented, including API endpoints and enrollment timelines.
- Risks identified (two‑week renewal delay, early‑upgrade incentive impact, legacy contract addenda) are recorded in the ticket description.
- Security review completed within 48 hours and executive sign‑off recorded by Jamal Osei.

## Investigation

A review of the revised draft‑review copy confirmed the three edge‑case scenarios flagged by Vera Becker on 2026‑01‑28. The policy now includes explicit language for enrollment lag, incentive protection, and contract addenda. The security team will need to verify that **SecureAuth (restricted folder)** can meet the required enrollment window without breaking existing authentication flows. Any gaps will be raised as comments on the ticket for engineering to address.

artifacts.summary: Recorded approval decision for MFA enforcement

items.text:
## Background

On 2026-02-05, a formal approval meeting was held to review the revised MFA policy. The policy incorporated three edge‑case scenarios flagged earlier by the Sales Lead on 2026‑01‑28: a potential two‑week renewal delay for accounts still on single‑factor login, risk to the 30‑day “early‑upgrade” incentive, and legacy contracts lacking explicit MFA clauses. The draft‑review copy and its revisions were stored in the restricted folder and only shared within the legal‑product circle. During the meeting, General Counsel **Aarav Tanaka** presented the final policy (restricted folder) and confirmed the go‑live date as **day 27 ** and the MFA provider as **SecureAuth (restricted folder)**. CEO **Jamal Osei** reviewed the compliance language, risk mitigations, and the security‑lead’s upcoming integration validation, then gave his final sign‑off.

## Recommendation

Approve the MFA enforcement rollout as outlined, with the go‑live scheduled for **day 27 ** and SecureAuth as the MFA provider (restricted folder). The rollout proceeds under the conditions that the security lead (Sofia Lopez) completes the integration review within 48 hours of ticket creation, and the implementation ticket **TKT-041‑M1A3** is updated with the final approval status by 2026‑02‑07.

## Conditions

- Security lead Sofia Lopez must validate SecureAuth integration within the stipulated 48‑hour window.
- Implementation ticket TKT‑041‑M1A3 must be updated with final approval status by 2026‑02‑07.
- All artifacts, including the final policy document, remain in the restricted folder and are not to be distributed outside the legal‑product circle.
